RimWarningTooltip: Rim style is approximate. A wheel style's effect on car mass is estimated from its lightness tier (an empirical COEF·D²·width formula), not taken directly from the game. Rim size and tyre width are exact; only the mass change from the wheel style is approximate. It is a difference of a few kg, so it has a negligible effect on the resulting tune.
CdTooltip: Drag coefficient. When both fields are filled, overrides mass/profile estimate. Typical: sports car 0.28–0.36, SUV 0.38–0.50.
FrontalAreaTooltip: Frontal cross-section area. Typical: sports car 1.8–2.1, SUV 2.5–3.2.
ConstraintHint: Set allowed ranges for springs, ride height and aero. Other parameters are automatically calculated within standard game limits.
DisciplineRoadTooltip: Road Racing — tarmac tracks, focus on handling and cornering speed.
DisciplineTougeTooltip: Touge — mountain pass, requires precise corner entry and stability.
DisciplineRallyTooltip: Rally — mixed surface, soft suspension and predictable behaviour.
DisciplineCrossCountryTooltip: Cross Country — full off-road, maximum suspension travel and durability.
DisciplineDriftTooltip: Drift — controlled oversteer, focus on angle and slip control.
DisciplineDragTooltip: Drag Racing — straight-line, maximum weight transfer at launch.
DisciplineStreetTooltip: Street Racing — urban tracks with civilian traffic. Speed and manoeuvrability.
SeasonSummerTooltip: Summer — dry hot tarmac, maximum grip. Standard baseline setup.
SeasonSpringTooltip: Spring — wet roads from cherry blossom rain, moderate grip reduction.
SeasonAutumnTooltip: Autumn — heavy rain, wet roads, longer braking distances. Softer setup.

PowerEstimatedHint: Estimate: the game files have no exact factory data for this swapped engine, so power and torque are approximated from the stock curve.
ResultMaxSpeedTooltip: ~ Estimated top speed at current gear ratios and RPM
ResultRecGearsHint: Recommended number of gears for this build — computed from the engine's powerband and the speed range it can actually reach. It's advice, not a copy of your installed gearbox, so it may differ. For the most out of the engine, fit a gearbox with this many speeds.
ResultForceRecGears: Override ratios & chart with recommended gears
ResultMaxRpmOverrideHint: Manually set the rev limiter used in every calculation (gearing, top speed, launch RPM). Overrides the calculated value until reset.
ResultOverrideEnableTooltip: Enable manual override — unchecking returns to the calculated value
ResultSpringOverrideHint: Manually set the min/max spring-rate range the calculator is allowed to use. Overrides the selected suspension part's own DB range while checked.
ResultRideHeightOverrideHint: Manually set the exact ride height used in every calculation. Overrides the calculated value while checked.
DrivingStyleAeroHint: Shifts front/rear downforce within the car's own aero range: Grip adds downforce (more cornering grip, more drag), Speed reduces it (less drag, higher top speed). Default (centre) keeps the discipline's own balance.
DrivingStyleChassisHint: Shifts every front/rear balance lever together — differential (incl. AWD centre split), ARB, springs, dampers, ride height (rake), tyre pressure, brake bias, camber, toe, and caster: Stable favours straight-line traction and understeer safety, Agile makes the car rotate more readily. Default (centre) keeps the discipline's own balance.
ResultSpringsHint: Spring rates are calculated from pure physics with no limits — they may exceed the in-game slider range. The game's limits depend on suspension geometry (motion ratio). Use as a starting point — fine-tune exact values in-game.
LaunchControlHint: Optimal launch RPM. Hold the throttle at this RPM before the green light.
HelpProgressLabel: 10 steps • Quick guide to Tune Master
HelpStep0Text:
The top bar of the main window contains all display controls — adjust these first for a comfortable experience.

• Language: Русский / English — switches the entire interface.
• Font «+» / «−» — changes the font size across the whole app (results, charts, part lists). Size is saved and restored on restart.
• Units: Metric ↔ Imperial — toggles all displayed values (speeds, pressures, lengths, spring rates).
• Power unit: HP / PS / kW — independent from the metric/imperial toggle.
• Spring-rate unit: N/mm · kgf/mm · lb/in — displayed on results and charts.
HelpStep0Note: All internal calculations always run in metric (SI) units. Units and language switches only affect the displayed text — the underlying physics remain unchanged. Font size, selected units and language are saved to %APPDATA%\ForzaTuneMaster\settings.json.
HelpStep1Text: Top-left, in the 'Car search' box, start typing a make, model or year — the list filters automatically. Select a car from the dropdown. All specifications (mass, weight distribution, power, torque, RPM, engine, drive type, gear count, wheelbase, tyres, etc.) are filled in automatically from the built-in game database. The '✕' button clears the selection.
HelpStep1Note: The entire car and parts database is bundled with the app and extracted directly from Forza Horizon 6 game files — no internet and no manual spec entry needed. The selected car appears in the header of the results panel on the right.
HelpStep2Text:
Below the search box are collapsible upgrade sections — just like the in-game garage. Click a header to expand a section:

• Body kits & modifications (swaps)
• Engine
• Chassis & handling
• Drivetrain
• Tyres & wheels
• Aero & appearance

Each section offers exactly the parts that exist for the selected car in the game.
HelpStep2Note: Part lists are built from the selected car's database; categories that don't apply auto-hide. Changing any part recalculates power, mass, drive type and geometry, and the tune updates automatically.
HelpStep3Text: The 'Body kits & modifications' section holds the swaps: engine, drivetrain (FWD/RWD/AWD) and aspiration type — these reshape the whole power map and car behaviour. The 'Engine' section is grouped: valvetrain & bottom end (camshaft, displacement, valves, pistons, flywheel), air/fuel/exhaust (intake, manifold, exhaust, fuel system, intercooler, restrictor) and ignition/cooling.
HelpStep3Note: For electric cars the ICE sections are hidden — a 'Motor & battery' section appears instead, with a motor swap and its upgrades. Hybrids and ICE cars use the engine sections.
HelpStep4Text: • CHASSIS — springs/dampers, anti-roll bars (front/rear), brakes, chassis stiffness, weight reduction. • DRIVETRAIN — gearbox, clutch, final drive/driveline, differential. • TYRES & WHEELS — tyre compound, width and profile (front/rear), wheel style and size, track spacers. • AERO — front bumper, rear wing, rear bumper, side skirts.
HelpStep4Note: The level of the installed parts sets the physical tuning limits: the generator selects values within the range that the chosen parts allow (e.g. race springs provide a wider stiffness and ride-height range). Wheels (rim style) — approximate: their effect on car mass is estimated from the wheel's lightness category (an empirical formula), not taken directly from the game. Rim size and tyre width are exact. It is a difference of a few kg, so it has a negligible effect on the tuning calculations.
HelpStep5Text:
At the bottom of the results panel (right), choose a discipline — it determines target spring frequencies, wheel geometry, gear ratios, differential and tyre pressure:

• Road • Touge • Rally • Cross Country • Drift • Drag • Street

Next to it, select a season (Spring / Summer / Autumn / Winter). For Drag, also set the distance (¼, ½ or mile).
HelpStep5Note: There is no separate 'Generate' button — the tune recalculates automatically with any change: car selection, a part swap, discipline or season. Season changes the grip factor and adjusts springs, dampers, ARB, differential and tyre pressure.
HelpStep6Text: The right panel shows the finished tune. The coloured bar under each value shows where it sits within its allowed range. Results are split into sections:
HelpStep7Text:
In Drag mode a '🚦 LAUNCH CONTROL' block appears above the gears with the optimal launch RPM. Hold the throttle at this RPM before launching.

The calculation accounts for: aspiration type (turbos need pre-spooling), torque-peak RPM (lower peak = lower launch), drive type (AWD can launch at higher RPM) and fuel type (diesel gets lower RPM).
HelpStep8Text:
Profiles save a full build: car, installed parts, discipline/season and the result.

• '💾 Save' — stores the current build. Name auto-generated: Make_Model_Year_Drive_Discipline.
• 'Load' — pick a profile from the list below and it applies instantly.
• '🗑 Delete' — removes the selected profile.
• 'Delete all' — clears the entire profile list.

Profiles are stored as JSON in %APPDATA%\ForzaTuneMaster\profiles\ and are recalculated automatically on load when required.
HelpStep8Note: Units and language toggle in the top bar: • Metric / Imperial — affects all unit displays • Power: HP / PS / kW • Spring rate: N/mm · kgf/mm · lb/in • Interface language: Русский / English • “+” / “−” buttons — font size across the whole app (charts included). Size is saved. All calculations run in metric (SI) units — imperial conversion is for display only.
HelpStep9Text:
Tune results can be shown in a separate window on top of the game and other apps:

• TOGGLE — use the 'Overlay' checkbox in the results panel header or press Ctrl+Shift+O
• DRAG — using the window header
• RESIZE — from any corner of the window
• OPACITY — adjust with the slider in the header
• CLOSE — click the ✕ button in the header or press Ctrl+Shift+O again

Overlay position, size and opacity are saved and restored when reopening.

💡 When you change the car or a part, the overlay charts (just like in the main window) update smoothly: fade-out → redraw → fade-in. Language/unit changes redraw instantly.
ChangelogV0: • FORCED-INDUCTION POWER FIX. Camshaft and intercooler upgrades no longer silently do nothing when added to a naturally-aspirated engine that's just getting its first turbo or supercharger from the Conversions menu — both now correctly add power. • DRAG STRIP GEARING. Launch-RPM tuning no longer wastes passes chasing a final-drive fit that undoes its own change. Gearboxes with more gears than a short strip's trap speed needs no longer get every gear crammed into a narrow band — the extra gears now extend past it as real overdrive ratios. Mile-distance gearing recalibrated against real in-game trap speeds. • TOP SPEED ACCURACY. Cars whose recorded top speed was limited by their stock gearbox (not by aerodynamics) no longer feed an incorrect drag coefficient into every speed and gearing calculation. • WEIGHT ACCOUNTING FIXES. Wheel-style weight no longer double-counts with a rim/tire size change on the same axle; intercooler weight is no longer disregarded for engines with no factory-stock intercooler tier; body-kit weight now applies correctly when loading a saved profile with a non-stock kit. • MANUAL OVERRIDES (NEW). Max RPM, spring rate min/max, and ride height can now be entered directly in the results panel, including a manual-gearbox mode that shifts to the rev limiter instead of leaving an automatic's safety margin. • UI FIXES & FRENCH LOCALISATION. The floating overlay now centres on screen instead of risking an off-screen position; override fields no longer shift the layout when toggled; carburettor engines show "Carburettor" instead of "Fuel System"; added a button to open the profiles folder. The app is now available in French.
HelpStep6Line1: • TYRE PRESSURE — front/rear. Based on tyre compound, adjusted according to mass and weight distribution.
HelpStep6Line2: • WHEEL ALIGNMENT — camber (discipline + load + aero), caster (mass + speed), toe (drive + discipline + speed).
HelpStep6Line3: • ANTI-ROLL BARS (ARB) — front/rear stiffness. Depends on discipline, mass, track, weight distribution and body roll.
HelpStep6Line4: • SPRINGS + RIDE HEIGHT — stiffness from target frequency (k = 0.0197 × Hz² × mass × wtDist) within the chosen springs' physics. Height: from discipline and engine position.
HelpStep6Line5: • DAMPERS — rebound/bump (1–20). Base from discipline, adjusted for mass, weight distribution, drive type and aspiration.
HelpStep6Line6: • AERODYNAMICS — front/rear downforce. Depends on drive type, speed and power; resolved iteratively. Drift/CC/Rally are reduced.
HelpStep6Line7: • DIFFERENTIAL — acceleration/deceleration lock. Based on discipline/drive, power and torque. For AWD — separate front and centre differential.
HelpStep6Line8: • BRAKES — balance (% front) = weight distribution + discipline offset. Pressure: based on discipline, mass and speed.
HelpStep6Line9: • GEARING — final drive targeting maximum speed, ratios (geometric progression) with post-validation. First/top gear from discipline.
HelpStep6Line10: Hover over any value — the tooltip explains the physics. Below: the gear chart (speed range per gear) with a legend (trajectory, rev limit, max speed) and the power/torque curve. The '!' badge next to springs warns that values may exceed in-game limits. Next to final drive — recommended gear count with a force-recalc checkbox. The checkboxes show/hide the charts. Charts animate smoothly when data changes.
ChartPeakToleranceHint: Calculated values. May differ slightly from in-game due to curve scaling mechanics and approximation.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Drag: Drag: neutral front (~32 PSI), minimum rear (~18-20 PSI) for maximum launch grip.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Drift: Drift: ~25 PSI front / ~22 PSI rear for predictable sliding.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Rally: Rally/CC: lower pressure for maximum contact patch.
Expl_TirePressureReason_CrossCountry: Rally/CC: lower pressure for maximum contact patch.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Touge: Touge: slightly softer than the base for mountain road grip.
Expl_TirePressureReason_Street: Street: standard pressure with a slight rear margin for manoeuvres.
Expl_CamberReason_Drag: Drag: minimal camber — maximum contact patch at launch.
Expl_CamberReason_Drift: Drift: aggressive front camber for control at high steering angles.
Expl_CamberReason_Rally: Rally: moderate camber — flat contact patch on gravel.
Expl_CamberReason_CrossCountry: CC: minimal camber — maximum contact on bumps.
Expl_CamberReason_Touge: Touge: increased camber for precise cornering on tight bends.
Expl_CamberReason_Road: Road: classic negative camber to compensate for body roll in corners.
Expl_ARBNote_Drag: Drag: minimal front for weight transfer; stiff rear for platform.
Expl_ARBNote_DriftRWD: Drift: soft front for initiation; moderate rear for angle hold (ForzaFire R20-25).
Expl_ARBNote_Rally: Rally: soft for independent wheel travel on gravel.
Expl_ARBNote_CrossCountry: CC: minimum stiffness for suspension articulation.
Expl_ARBNote_TougeRWD: Touge RWD: stiffer for precise control.
Expl_ARBNote_TougeFWD: Touge FWD: soft front for grip, stiff rear for rotation.
Expl_ARBNote_StreetFWD: Street FWD: soft front for grip, stiffer rear to counter understeer.
Expl_ARBNote_RoadRWD: Road RWD: front stiffer than rear for precise entry (ForzaFire F18-28/R12-20).
Expl_ARBNote_RoadFWD: Road FWD: soft front (grip), stiffer rear (rotation).
Expl_ARBNote_RoadAWD: Road AWD: F26/R33 — balanced ARBs (ForzaFire F22-30/R28-38).
Expl_Springs_Fmt: Springs: F {0} / R {1} N/mm ({2:F2}/{3:F2} Hz, suspension {4}).
Expl_Springs_Defaults_Fmt: Springs: F {0} / R {1} N/mm (default values, tuning unavailable).
Expl_RideHeightNote_Drag: Drag: minimum clearance for aero, low CG; slight rear rake for weight transfer at launch.
Expl_RideHeightNote_Drift: Drift: low ride height for stability in slides.
Expl_RideHeightNote_Rally: Rally: high clearance for uneven terrain.
Expl_RideHeightNote_CrossCountry: CC: maximum clearance for jumps and bumps.
Expl_RideHeightNote_Road: Road: minimum clearance for low CG.
Expl_RideHeightNote_Touge: Touge: low ride height with slight rear rake for rotation.
Expl_RideHeightNote_Street: Street: low ride height with a small margin for road imperfections.
Expl_Dampers_Fmt: Rebound: F {0} / R {1}, bump: F {2} / R {3}. (bump/rebound: F {4:F0}%, R {5:F0}%)
Expl_Dampers_Defaults_Fmt: Dampers: rebound F {0} / R {1}, bump F {2} / R {3} (default values).
Expl_Aero_Fmt: Downforce: F {0} / R {1} kg. {2} km/h, {3} hp.
Expl_AeroNote_Drag: Drag: minimum downforce for top speed.
Expl_AeroNote_Drift: Drift: minimum downforce for free sliding.
Expl_AeroNote_CrossCountry: CC: minimum downforce to avoid catching the terrain.
Expl_AeroNote_Street: Street: high downforce with a small top-speed reserve.
Expl_AeroNote_RoadFWD: Road FWD: front downforce for grip.
Expl_Differential_AWDFmt: Main diff: accel {0}%, decel {1}%. Front: accel {2}%, decel {3}%, centre {4}% (rear). {5}
Expl_Differential_FmtAccelOnly: Main diff: accel {0}% (Sport LSD — no decel slider). {1}
Expl_Differential_AWDFmtAccelOnly: Main diff: accel {0}%. Front: accel {1}%, centre {2}% (rear). Sport LSD — no decel sliders. {3}
Expl_BrakesReason_Drag: Rear bias — minimal intervention at launch.
Expl_FinalDrive_MultiGear: FD {0}. Ratios: {1}. Target {2} km/h, actual {3} km/h @ {4} rpm. {5}
Expl_FinalDrive_Warning: ⚠ RPM below torque band (< {0:F0}) on shifts: {1}.
